experiment: Balanced-beta intervention on gap-induced RAdam divergence
task: P0: does balancing beta1=beta2 reduce the gap-induced R_opt?

git.note: analysis_code_commit is the exact PR head containing the analysis code and generated result artifacts before later documentation/provenance-only tightening commits

protocol.gradient_sequence: Same real paired {G_t^1.0, G_t^1.3}_{t=1..20} from the frozen #49 Arm-A checkpoints (k32/k64/k128/k256, same seed-3 trajectory)
protocol.starting_point: Uniform for all beta configs: m0=0, v0=0, step0=0. The real extracted state is never used (no old-beta history + new-beta step mixing).
protocol.effective_support: top 1% of coordinates by |u1| for h_i/Disp only; R_opt is computed over the full vector

trajectory.raw_inputs: analysis/real_history/{k}/grad_history_1.npy and grad_history_g.npy; SHA256 and checkpoint bindings are recorded in analysis/crossk_scalar_history/raw_manifest.json

validation.replay: pure-numpy float32 RAdam (analysis/numpy_radam.py), previously validated against stored torch histories in the cross-K pipeline
validation.committed_h20_test: tests/test_balanced_beta_h20.py recomputes effective-support h_i statistics from committed raw_h20 arrays
validation.full_vector_R_opt_boundary: full-vector R_opt requires the large hash-identified external gradient histories and is not independently recomputable from the small committed h_i arrays alone

environment.analysis_runtime: Python 3.6.8 + NumPy 1.19.5 on the project compute server
